I’m going to fix the SQL script to use the correct column name in the `pg_policies` system view (`policyname` instead of `polname`) so it runs on Supabase/Postgres without errors. Then I’ll answer your question briefly and include the corrected SQL snippets.

---



---

- pg_policies is a PostgreSQL system catalog view that lists all Row-Level Security (RLS) policies defined on tables.
- The correct column for the policy name is policyname (not polname). Your error is because the script referenced a non-existent column.

Use this corrected SQL (only the policy existence checks changed):

```sql
-- Allow authenticated users to read roles
do $$ begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'roles_read'
  ) then
    create policy roles_read on public.roles for select to authenticated using (true);
  end if;
end $$;

-- Allow authenticated users to insert roles (adjust later if needed)
do $$ begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'roles_insert'
  ) then
    create policy roles_insert on public.roles for insert to authenticated with check (true);
  end if;
end $$;
```

If needed, you can inspect existing policies with:
- List policies on roles:
  - select policyname, schemaname, tablename, cmd, roles from pg_policies where tablename = 'roles' | cat

Summary
- pg_policies: system view of RLS policies.
- Correct column: policyname.
- I updated `Database Schema Creation SQL Scripts/UserRoles-Schema.sql` to use policyname so it runs cleanly.

- Meaning: Your update ran, but the API couldn’t return a single JSON row. Most often this happens because RLS allows UPDATE but blocks SELECT on the same table, so the “returning” row can’t be read.

What I changed
- The edit save no longer requires a returned row; it updates then reloads the list. This avoids the error message.

Fix RLS so updates and reads work
- If you want admins to edit anyone and everyone else to only edit their own profile:
```sql
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

-- Read: let authenticated users read profiles (adjust as needed)
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_select_auth') then
    create policy profiles_select_auth on public.profiles
      for select to authenticated
      using (true);
  end if;
end $$;

-- Update own profile
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_update_self') then
    create policy profiles_update_self on public.profiles
      for update to authenticated
      using (auth.uid() = id)
      with check (auth.uid() = id);
  end if;
end $$;

-- Optional: allow a specific admin role to update anyone (replace 'Admin' as needed)
-- Assumes profiles.role stores the role name
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_update_admins') then
    create policy profiles_update_admins on public.profiles
      for update to authenticated
      using (exists (
               select 1 from public.profiles p
               where p.id = auth.uid() and p.role = 'Admin'
             ))
      with check (true);
  end if;
end $$;
```

- If you just need quick functionality for now (less secure), allow all authenticated users to update and select:
```sql
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_select_all_auth') then
    create policy profiles_select_all_auth on public.profiles
      for select to authenticated using (true);
  end if;
end $$;

do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_update_all_auth') then
    create policy profiles_update_all_auth on public.profiles
      for update to authenticated using (true) with check (true);
  end if;
end $$;
```

Next steps
- Apply one of the policy sets above, wait a few seconds for cache to refresh, then retry editing a user.

### What you want
- Users can edit only their own profile details (name, email, phone), not their role.
- “All Users” and “User Role Config” visible/accessible only to Admins.

### Recommended setup

- Backend (Supabase/Postgres) is the source of truth. Enforce permissions with RLS.
- Frontend does conditional rendering and route-guarding for UX only. Never rely on it for security.

#### 1) Supabase RLS on public.profiles
Use policies that:
- Let everyone read profiles (or narrow as needed).
- Let a user update only their own row, but NOT the `role`.
- Let admins update any row, including `role`.

SQL (run in Supabase SQL editor):
```sql
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

-- 1) Read policy (adjust as needed)
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_select_auth') then
    create policy profiles_select_auth on public.profiles
      for select to authenticated
      using (true);
  end if;
end $$;

-- 2) Update self (role must remain unchanged)
-- WITH CHECK runs on the new row; we compare against the current DB role for the same user
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_update_self_details') then
    create policy profiles_update_self_details on public.profiles
      for update to authenticated
      using (auth.uid() = id)
      with check (
        auth.uid() = id
        and role = (select role from public.profiles p where p.id = auth.uid())
      );
  end if;
end $$;

-- 3) Admin updates (can update any user, including role)
-- Assumes admin is determined by their profile.role = 'Admin' (case-insensitive)
do $$ begin
  if not exists (select 1 from pg_policies where policyname = 'profiles_update_admins') then
    create policy profiles_update_admins on public.profiles
      for update to authenticated
      using (
        exists (
          select 1 from public.profiles me
          where me.id = auth.uid() and lower(me.role) = 'admin'
        )
      )
      with check (true);
  end if;
end $$;
```

Notes:
- This prevents non-admins from changing their own `role` while allowing Admins to modify anyone’s `role`.
- Keep `profiles.role` consistent (e.g., enforce lower-cased values) or migrate to a `role_id` FK later.

#### 2) Frontend route and menu gating (UX)
- Hide menu items for non-admins
- Block admin-only routes

Example: Admin-only wrapper
```tsx
// components/auth/RequireAdmin.tsx
import { Navigate, useLocation } from "react-router-dom"
import { useAuthContext } from "../../context/AuthContext"

export function RequireAdmin({ children }: { children: JSX.Element }) {
  const { profile } = useAuthContext()
  const location = useLocation()
  if (!profile || String(profile.role).toLowerCase() !== "admin") {
    return <Navigate to="/error-404" state={{ from: location }} replace />
  }
  return children
}
```

Usage in routing:
```tsx
// App.tsx
<Route path="users" element={
  <ProtectedRoute>
    <RequireAdmin><Users /></RequireAdmin>
  </ProtectedRoute>
} />
<Route path="user-roles" element={
  <ProtectedRoute>
    <RequireAdmin><RoleConfig /></RequireAdmin>
  </ProtectedRoute>
} />
```

Hide sidebar items:
```tsx
// layout/AppSidebar.tsx
import { useAuthContext } from "../context/AuthContext"

function AppSidebar() {
  const { profile } = useAuthContext()
  const isAdmin = String(profile?.role).toLowerCase() === "admin"

  const filteredNavItems = useMemo(() => {
    return navItems.map(item => {
      if (item.name === "User Management" && !isAdmin) return null
      return item
    }).filter(Boolean)
  }, [isAdmin])

  // render filteredNavItems instead of navItems
}
```

#### 3) Edit Profile screen (self-service)
- Build a separate “My Profile” screen where the user can update first name, last name, email, and phone.
- Do not show or send `role` from that form. The RLS already protects it; the UI avoids confusion.

### Potential pitfalls with relying on the client’s role
- Security: Client-side checks are bypassable. Always enforce RLS on the database.
- Stale role: If role changes server-side, the client might have a cached role. Re-fetch profile on auth state changes and on protected route entry.
- Case/typo drift: Storing `role` as free text risks “Admin” vs “admin”. Standardize (e.g., lower-case) and/or migrate to `role_id` referencing `roles(id)`.
- Propagation: If you put role in JWT custom claims, claims may not update until token refresh. Using live `profiles` lookups in RLS avoids that.
- Mixed policies: Allowing UPDATE but not SELECT on the same table can cause “no row returned” after update. Make sure both are aligned for your UX flow.

### Minimal changes to your current code
- Keep the UI checks for role to hide routes and menu items.
- Add the RLS policies above so non-admins can’t change their `role` even if they try.
- Build a simple “My Profile” page for self-updates (no role field).
- Optionally normalize `profiles.role` to lower-case and later consider a `role_id` FK to `roles`.
